title: MaxiMin Active Learning in Overparameterized Model Classes
review_status: full-text audit complete; one-dimensional binary label-complexity result with narrow target assumptions, illustrative MNIST comparison, and stated query-computation bottleneck
sections_checked: minimum-norm interpolation query criterion
one-dimensional binary piecewise-constant bisection theorem and label bound
kernel and neural-network simulations
1,000-image binary MNIST test-error comparison against random queries
conclusion on computational bottleneck and open multiclass/regression cases
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2019-05-29; v2 dated 2020-04-28; full arXiv HTML audited. Frame stratification is by first arXiv submission.
evidence_note: Proves an O(k log N) label bound for a one-dimensional binary piecewise-constant target with appropriately scaled regions under a two-layer ReLU minimum-norm interpolator; tests MNIST on 1,000 vectorized images under a binary digit split and compares test error to random sampling. The paper flags query computation as a bottleneck and leaves multiclass/regression/other learners open.

title: Gradient-Based Neural DAG Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; nonlinear score-based DAG recovery tested under identifiability assumptions, non-convex optimization, and substantial runtime cost
sections_checked: observational DAG identifiability and no-hidden-variable assumptions
nonlinear Gaussian additive-noise model scope
acyclicity constraint and non-convex optimization procedure
synthetic and real-data comparison using SHD and SID
runtime appendix and comparison to NOTEARS
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2019-06-05; v2 full text identifies ICLR 2020 publication; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: GraN-DAG reports SHD and causal SID and performs strongly against continuous baselines, competitively with CAM/GSF in evaluated settings. Exact graph identification relies on assumptions such as no hidden variables and identifiable nonlinear Gaussian ANMs; practical optimization is non-convex/stationary-point based. Runtime appendix reports about 10 vs 1 minutes at 20 nodes and 4 vs 1 hours at 100 nodes versus NOTEARS on the described setup; GPU roughly halves 100-node time.

title: An Active Learning Approach for Reducing Annotation Cost in Skin Lesion Analysis
review_status: full-text audit complete; two-task ISIC result suggests label savings, with a strong negative augmentation ablation and limited external scope
sections_checked: uncertainty and representativeness selection plus image aggregation method
ISIC 2017 two-task dataset and train/validation/test composition
same-budget random/AIFT/full-data results and metrics
50%/40% label use and statistical stopping rule
mix-up augmentation counterexample and leaderboard comparability exclusions
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2019-09-05; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: On two ISIC 2017 tasks, reports near-full-data accuracy using 50% and 40% of the labeled pool (task 1 0.860 vs 0.863 full; task 2 0.908 vs 0.903 full). The same-budget SA+Mix-up ablation collapses on several measures (task-1 accuracy 0.467; task-2 sensitivity 0.124), unlike SA+AS. Evidence is two tasks in one dataset/archive setting, not prospective cross-clinic validation.

title: Distribution inference risks: Identifying and mitigating sources of leakage
review_status: full-text audit complete; causal-feature protection shown for a defined synthetic distributional-membership attack, not general privacy protection
sections_checked: distribution inference threat and adversary formalization
leakage-source analysis
four-party synthetic causal/spurious-feature example with 512 records each
causal ERM, associational ERM and IRM in-distribution versus shifted-test results
scope of causal mitigation and released attack library
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2022-09-19; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: A constructed four-party, 512-record-per-party example shows an associational model can expose a distributional membership signal through a spurious feature, while a model using the true causal parent avoids that signal; under flipped test correlation causal ERM generalizes better than associational ERM while the in-distribution ordering reverses. This is a specific modeled attack and assumed causal feature structure, not a general privacy guarantee.

title: Consistent Training via Energy-Based GFlowNets for Modeling Discrete Joint Distributions
review_status: full-text audit complete; peptide active-learning score trades off against diversity and novelty under a computational oracle
sections_checked: joint energy-based GFlowNet objective
synthetic conditional-generation failure mode and comparison
single-round antimicrobial-peptide score/diversity/novelty table
ten-round active-learning protocol and oracle threshold
limitations of discrete-only candidates and absence of wet-lab validation
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2022-10-31; v2 dated 2022-11-02; NeurIPS 2022 workshop version; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: In a ten-round peptide active-learning simulation with 1,000 oracle-scored candidates per round, DynaPPO has highest score (0.938), while JEB-GFN obtains greater diversity (31.83 vs 22.34 for GFlowNet-AL) but lower score (0.922 vs 0.932) and novelty (24.26 vs 28.44). Scores are computational-oracle outcomes, not prospective wet-lab validation; sequence values are discrete only.

title: Improve ROI with Causal Learning and Conformal Prediction
review_status: full-text audit complete; three of four reported short randomized online settings show significant revenue improvement, with one explicit null exception and platform-specific scope
sections_checked: DRP covariate-shift and low-sample problem statement
MC-dropout plus conformal calibration scope
offline AUCC across three uplift datasets and four settings
four five-day randomized online tests with equal reward budgets
online result exception and deployment limitations
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2024-07-01; full arXiv HTML audited.
evidence_note: rDRP calibrates the MC-dropout uncertainty of the DRP model; paper reports three public offline uplift datasets and four online five-day randomized three-arm tests on an incentivized-advertising platform with equal reward budgets. Authors state significant revenue improvement in three of four conditions, with sufficient data/no shift as the exception. Evidence is a single commercial platform/mechanism; not a generic conformal guarantee for all causal/uplift estimators.

title: Casual Inference via Style Bias Deconfounding for Domain Generalization
review_status: full-text audit complete; benchmark evidence for style-deconfounding modules is generally positive but varies by domain and does not establish real-world causal identification
sections_checked: paper's SCM/style-confounder framing and back-door feature-fusion construction
single- and multi-domain classification tables
natural and medical image segmentation results
module and hyperparameter ablations
domain-specific counterexamples and causal-interpretation boundary
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-03-21; title/index term spells ‘Casual’; full arXiv HTML audited.
evidence_note: SDCL improves many benchmark averages/ablations (e.g. PACS single-domain classification 68.07 to 71.00 for the listed base versus full method), but not every domain cell improves (e.g. UDP PACS art-domain score 78.61 to 75.40 despite average improving from 66.37 to 67.83). Benchmark results support a method-specific generalization claim, not proof that latent styles are the true causes or that real-world causal interventions were performed.

title: Weak Form Scientific Machine Learning: Test Function Construction for System Identification
review_status: full-text audit complete; data-driven weak-form radius selection improves runtime in several simulated systems but parameter-error alignment fails in identified high-noise cases
sections_checked: estimated quadrature-error changepoint and critical radius construction
four ODE test systems and 100-run experimental protocol
noise, polynomial-order, and temporal-resolution sensitivity
SL versus MG parameter-error/runtime comparison
high-noise OLS/IRLS counterexamples and real-data scope
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-07-03; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: Across logistic growth, Duffing, Lorenz and FitzHugh–Nagumo simulations with 100 trials per setting, SL is often faster than MG (reported IRLS median-runtime improvements about 60–70% on several systems). Critical radius does not always coincide with minimum parameter error: high-noise OLS logistic/FitzHugh–Nagumo and high-noise cubic FitzHugh–Nagumo under IRLS are counterexamples. Evaluation is canonical simulated ODEs, not real experimental time series.

title: A Unified Theory for Causal Inference: Direct Debiased Machine Learning via Bregman-Riesz Regression
review_status: full-text audit complete; synthesis/tutorial note connecting estimators under explicit ATE identification and model/loss assumptions, not an independent empirical comparison
sections_checked: ATE target and unconfoundedness/positivity/boundedness assumptions
Riesz representer and Neyman-orthogonal score connections
Bregman-Riesz, covariate balancing, DRE, TMLE and matching relationships
linear versus logistic/model-loss duality
conclusion and citation of companion theory/simulation papers
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-10-30; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: The note unifies Riesz regression, balancing, density-ratio estimation, TMLE and matching for ATE and recommends entropy balancing plus TMLE; it explicitly states identification assumptions and model/loss-dependent relationships. It summarizes companion Kato papers for detailed theory/simulations and does not itself provide an independent new empirical head-to-head result.

title: An Active Learning Algorithm for Ranking from Pairwise Preferences with an Almost Optimal Query Complexity
review_status: full-text audit complete; provable adaptive preference-query savings relative to the same downstream rank learner, not an empirical reduction in human labeling time or absolute ranking error
sections_checked: pairwise tournament preference model including possible non-transitivity
relative-regret objective against all-pairs labels for a fixed downstream learner
epsilon-good decomposition and query-complexity theorem
SVM/large-margin learner reduction
query-versus-computation and NP-hard MFAST distinction
venue_year_verified: arXiv identifier first submitted in 2010; v11 PDF header dated 2011-05-17 and author manuscript dated 2019-07-01; full arXiv PDF audited. Frame period follows first submission.
evidence_note: Adaptive sampling reduces pair-label queries relative to an all-pairs learner under a relative-regret guarantee; the decomposition routine uses O(epsilon^-6 n log^5 n) expected queries with constant probability, and the SVM subsampling construction uses O(n polylog(n, epsilon^-1)) labels. Guarantee concerns label/query complexity, not human-time savings or correctness of potentially cyclic preferences. MFAST is NP-hard and query and solver computation remain distinct.

title: Visual Causal Feature Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; model-relative causal-coarsening theorem and simple synthetic/MNIST manipulator demonstrations, not broad real-vision causal validation
sections_checked: visual cause/macro-variable definition and causal/observational partition distinction
Causal Coarsening Theorem and its generative-family assumptions
causal-data/intervention requirement for learning representative manipulations
synthetic GRATING task error trajectory
MNIST Mechanical Turk manipulator experiment and manipulation-distance tradeoff
discussion of intended scope and appendix counterexamples
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2014-12-07; v2 revised 2015-06-04; frame period follows first submission; full arXiv PDF audited.
evidence_note: For its specified generative model family, proves that almost all models induce a causal partition coarser than the observational partition. Assumptions include temporal ordering (image precedes behavior) and that the behavior is not represented in the image; learning manipulations still uses causal data on representative images. In synthetic GRATING, manipulator error falls from about 40% initially to about 6% after iterative training; MNIST uses Amazon Mechanical Turk judgments. Authors explicitly scope this as theory/algorithm feasibility on simple vision problems, not advanced CV deployment; real-world causal identification is not established by the observational coarsening result alone.
